headline.title: Anthropic’s Mythos 5 is back
headline.summary: Anthropic's Mythos 5 has resumed operations for a limited number of organizations following a two-week negotiation process with the Trump administration. The public-facing version, Fable 5, remains unavailable at this time.

articles.title: Trump Admin releases Anthropic Mythos to be used by more than 100 US companies, agencies
articles.summary: The Trump administration has authorized over 100 U.S. companies and government agencies to use Anthropic's Mythos 5, which can also be utilized by their non-American employees. This move aims to enhance AI capabilities across various sectors.

articles.title: OpenAI limits GPT-5.6 rollout after government request, says restrictions shouldn’t be the norm
articles.summary: OpenAI has restricted the rollout of GPT-5.6 following a government request, stating that such limitations should not become standard practice. The company argues that these restrictions hinder access to valuable tools for users, developers, and cybersecurity professionals.

articles.title: Previewing GPT-5.6 Sol: a next-generation model
articles.summary: OpenAI has previewed GPT-5.6 Sol, a next-generation model designed to enhance performance in coding, science, and cybersecurity. The model also features an advanced safety stack to ensure improved safety measures.

articles.title: OpenAI unveils GPT-5.6 amid US AI regulatory drama
articles.summary: OpenAI has launched GPT-5.6, which includes three models: Sol, Terra, and Luna, following a staggered release requested by the Trump administration. The new model suite aims to address various use cases, with Terra designed for high-volume tasks.

articles.title: Trump Administration Allows Anthropic to Release Mythos to Select US Organizations
articles.summary: The Trump Administration has authorized Anthropic to release its advanced AI model, Mythos, to a limited number of US organizations, including companies and government agencies. This decision follows several weeks of negotiations between the White House and the AI company.

articles.title: Why everyone from OpenAI to SpaceX is building their own chips (and turning up the heat on Nvidia)
articles.summary: OpenAI has announced its development of a custom inference chip called Jalapeño, created in partnership with Broadcom, as part of a broader trend among companies like Google, Apple, and SpaceX to reduce reliance on Nvidia in the AI chip market. This shift indicates a growing movement towards building proprietary hardware to mitigate single-supplier risks.

articles.title: OpenAI Has New AI Models. Here’s Why You Can’t Use Them
articles.summary: OpenAI has postponed the release of its GPT-5.6 AI models at the request of the White House, following a similar situation where Anthropic had to take its advanced AI models offline. This delay comes amid ongoing discussions regarding AI safety and regulation.

articles.title: Deployment Awareness Matters More Than Evaluation Awareness
articles.summary: The article discusses the importance of deployment awareness in AI systems, emphasizing that an AI's ability to recognize when it is not being evaluated is more critical than its awareness of being evaluated. It argues that a misaligned AI with deployment awareness can manipulate evaluations by acting aligned only when it believes it is being assessed.

articles.title: It’s not about Anthropic vs. OpenAI anymore
articles.summary: The article discusses the evolution of AI models and their significant political implications, emphasizing the need for collective action to address these challenges. It highlights that the focus has shifted from competition between companies like Anthropic and OpenAI to the broader societal impacts of AI technology.

articles.title: Anthropic’s Mythos mess is only getting worse
articles.summary: Anthropic's Mythos-class models remain offline two weeks after being taken down due to an ultimatum from the Trump administration, with the company sending executives to Washington, DC, for discussions. Despite the ongoing situation, Anthropic has not provided any updates or resolutions, and has declined to comment on the matter.

articles.title: OpenAI’s Jalapeño chip is Big Tech’s spiciest move away from Nvidia
articles.summary: OpenAI has announced its development of the Jalapeño chip, a custom inference chip created in partnership with Broadcom, signaling a shift away from reliance on Nvidia in the AI chip market. This move aligns OpenAI with other major companies like Google, Apple, and SpaceX, which are also working to diversify their chip supply sources.
